01 / THE IDEA

Closer to the machine.
Without losing the program.

A layout, a pointer, a calling convention. These decisions change what a program does. nC makes them part of the language, with contracts that stay visible across its levels.

Types and control flow must remain coherent through parsing, semantic analysis, IR, lowering and linking. Memory stays explicit and manual.

Why nC exists ↗

A LANGUAGE IN THE MAKING

Open development.
Documented limits.

The public edition is bootstrap V81. Its recorded B/C reconstructions are byte-identical within each tested host. The native command set is partial; global Stage3 promotion remains open.

Review the evidence ↗Release notes ↗

05 / BEFORE YOU BUILD

A few things
to know.

Do I need Rust or LLVM?

The native kit includes the compiler and provider required for the first program. Building retained Stage0 from source has separate Rust, seed and archiver requirements.

Which systems have been tested?

The V81 kit was tested on Windows x86-64 and Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL x86-64. Linux requires glibc 2.34 symbols or later. Other profiles have separate documented scopes.

Does type checking provide memory safety?

nC has manual/raw semantics. The program controls allocation, address validity and release. Type checking does not add ownership or implicit pointer-lifetime checks.

How can I contribute?

A useful bug report includes minimal source, the complete command, host, compiler and provider digests, diagnostic and expected result. Read the contribution guide before proposing a language change.
